column1: # Prompt routing table — prompt shape → the best-suited command.
# The file-signal table (rules.tsv) answers "you edited this file, load this skill".
# This one answers a different question: "you asked for THIS, another command fits it
# better than the one that would otherwise nudge you." Arbitration is by explicit
# priority, not by which hook the harness happened to schedule first.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   pattern         ERE, matched case-insensitively against the head of the prompt
#   command         the slash command to suggest (must exist under plugins/*/commands/)
#   owning_plugin   the rule only fires when this plugin is installed
#   priority        integer; highest match wins, ties broken by row order (first wins)
#   reason          why this command fits — shown to the user, so write it for them
# Adding a route is a data row, never a code change: route-prompt.sh carries no
# literal command names and validate.sh fails the build if it grows one.
# Priority bands, so a new row lands somewhere defensible:
#   90+   the ask names a deliverable a whole pipeline exists for
#   70-89 a specialist command clearly beats the generic one
#   40-69 a decent fit, but a general run would not be wrong
#   1-39  fallbacks — only fire when nothing more specific matched
# pattern
